title: NexaFlow
description: High-throughput event streaming platform in Go. Handles 50k+ events/sec with custom TCP framing and at-least-once delivery guarantees.
features: Our backend generated millions of domain events per day with no durable, replayable delivery mechanism. Kafka was cost-prohibitive at the scale we needed; SQS lacked the replay semantics required for audit trails.

Built NexaFlow in Go — a lightweight streaming server with a custom binary framing protocol over TCP, consumer groups with offset tracking in PostgreSQL, and a backpressure-aware producer SDK. Deployed as a 3-node cluster on GCP Cloud Run with persistent volumes.
Replaced three ad-hoc webhook pipelines and two cron-based polling loops. Incident recovery time dropped from hours to seconds — consumers replay from any offset instantly.

title: OrbitCMS
description: Headless CMS: Laravel API backend, Next.js admin dashboard, GraphQL interface. Powers 12 production sites across three different design systems.
features: Client teams were managing content in 4 different systems (WordPress, Strapi, raw DB scripts, CSV uploads). Consolidation was blocked because each site had unique content schemas and delivery requirements.

Designed a schema-on-write headless CMS with a dynamic field registry. Laravel provides a REST + GraphQL dual API; Next.js admin renders field editors from schema JSON. Multi-tenant from day one: each site gets isolated content namespaces under one DB with row-level security.
Migrated 12 production sites over 6 months with zero downtime. Content editors report 3× faster publishing. Developer onboarding for a new site type dropped from 2 weeks to 2 days.

title: CloudVault
description: End-to-end encrypted object storage on AWS S3. Zero-knowledge architecture with per-user key derivation (PBKDF2) and a Vue.js client.
features: Standard cloud storage (Dropbox, Google Drive, S3 with SSE) encrypts at rest using provider-managed keys — meaning the provider can technically read your data. We needed provable zero-knowledge storage.

Client-side AES-256-GCM encryption before upload. Each user's encryption key is derived from their passphrase using PBKDF2 (310,000 iterations, SHA-256), never sent to the server. Go backend handles upload orchestration and presigned S3 URLs. Vue.js SPA manages the WebCrypto API calls.
Work in progress. Alpha deployed with 3 design partners. Storage costs 40% cheaper than commercial alternatives at equivalent durability.

title: PGShield
description: Open-source Postgres query firewall. Sits between app and DB, detecting anomalous query patterns via statistical baseline + alerting.
features: SQL injection and credential compromise are the most common causes of database breaches — yet most Postgres deployments have no runtime query inspection layer. pgBouncer handles pooling; nothing handles threat detection.

PGShield is a transparent TCP proxy in Go that speaks the PostgreSQL wire protocol. It builds a rolling statistical baseline (query fingerprints, frequencies, execution times) per application role. Queries outside 3σ of normal trigger configurable actions: log, alert (Slack/PagerDuty webhook), or block.
Running in production at 2 companies with zero false-positive blocks in 6 months. Caught a compromised service account query pattern in staging before promotion.

title: CFWorker Kit
description: TypeScript toolkit for Cloudflare Workers: type-safe routing, middleware chains, and first-class KV/R2/D1 bindings. 1.2k GitHub stars.
architecture: ├── Router       — typed path params, method matching
└── Types        — full Cloudflare Workers env types
features: Cloudflare Workers' raw API is powerful but ergonomically rough — route matching, request/response typing, and binding wiring all require boilerplate. Existing frameworks were either too opinionated or lacked proper TypeScript generics.

Designed a minimal, zero-dependency toolkit: a typed router that infers path params, a composable middleware stack (same pattern as Express but with proper TS inference), and factory helpers for KV, R2, and D1 that surface binding errors at compile time.
Published on npm. 1.2k GitHub stars, 14k weekly downloads. Used in 3 of my own production projects and by the Cloudflare Workers community.

title: RedisWatcher
description: Real-time Redis monitoring dashboard in Vue.js. Visualizes memory footprint, keyspace events, and slow query logs via WebSocket streaming.
features: Redis's built-in CLI tools (redis-cli monitor, SLOWLOG, INFO) are powerful but not friendly to share across teams or view historically. Existing GUIs (RedisInsight) are heavy Electron apps that can't be self-hosted behind auth.

Lightweight web dashboard: a Go backend subscribes to Redis keyspace notifications and SLOWLOG polling, streams events over WebSocket to a Vue.js SPA. Charts use plain SVG — no chart library — for a tiny bundle. Entire stack ships as a single Docker image.
Work in progress. Used internally; planning open-source release after adding multi-instance support.
